questions.question: In graph databases, the connections between nodes.
questions.explanation: Edges or relationships connect nodes and represent associations between entities.

questions.question: Cassandra's consistency level where all replicas must acknowledge a write.
questions.explanation: The ALL consistency level requires all replica nodes to acknowledge before returning success.

questions.question: Cassandra's consistency level requiring a quorum of replicas to respond.
questions.explanation: QUORUM requires a majority of replicas to respond for read or write operations.

questions.question: The protocol MongoDB uses for ensuring replica set consistency.
questions.explanation: MongoDB uses a Raft-based consensus protocol for leader election and data consistency in replica sets.

questions.question: Graph query language used by Neo4j.
questions.explanation: Cypher is Neo4j's declarative graph query language for pattern matching in graphs.

questions.question: A consistency model where reads may not reflect the most recent write.
questions.explanation: Eventual consistency sacrifices immediate consistency for better availability and partition tolerance.

questions.question: Amazon's highly available key-value store using eventual consistency.
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is Amazon's fully managed NoSQL database service with eventual consistency by default.

questions.question: The technique of storing related data together to minimize queries.
questions.explanation: Denormalization in NoSQL duplicates data to optimize read performance and reduce joins.

questions.question: Column-family database developed at Facebook, later open-sourced.
questions.explanation: Cassandra was developed at Facebook and is now an Apache project designed for high scalability.

questions.question: The NoSQL database property of scaling by adding more machines.
questions.explanation: Horizontal scalability allows NoSQL systems to scale out by adding more commodity servers.

questions.question: Under the CAP theorem, which property does a CP system sacrifice during a network partition?
questions.explanation: CP systems preserve consistency by refusing or failing requests during partitions.

questions.question: Cassandra write consistency level that succeeds once a single replica acknowledges.
questions.explanation: Consistency level ONE requires acknowledgment from only one replica, favoring availability.

questions.question: The MongoDB routing process that directs queries to the correct shards.
questions.explanation: mongos instances route client queries to shards using the config server metadata.

questions.question: Cassandra's peer-to-peer protocol for exchanging node state and failure information.
questions.explanation: Nodes periodically gossip state with random peers to discover topology and failures.

questions.question: Technique used in Amazon's Dynamo to detect and reconcile concurrent versions of an object.
questions.explanation: Vector clocks capture per-node version history so conflicts can be detected and resolved.

questions.question: A Cassandra cluster has replication factor N = 3. For a workload using write consistency W and read consistency R to guarantee strong consistency, what inequality must hold?
alternatives: W plus R must exceed N
questions.explanation: When the write and read quorums overlap (W + R > N), every read set intersects the latest write set, so reads observe the most recent acknowledged write.

questions.question: In a sharded MongoDB cluster, chunks grow beyond the configured size and must be redistributed across shards. Which background process migrates chunks to keep shards balanced?
questions.explanation: MongoDB's balancer runs on the config server primary and migrates chunks between shards to equalize data distribution.

questions.question: A Redis-backed leaderboard must keep members ordered by score and support ZRANGE and ZREVRANK queries. Which Redis data structure is the right choice?
questions.explanation: Redis sorted sets pair each member with a score and keep them ordered, giving O(log N) rank and range operations ideal for leaderboards.

questions.question: A mobile app writes a profile update to replica A, then immediately reads from replica B and sees the old value. Which session consistency guarantee has been violated?
questions.explanation: Read-your-writes consistency guarantees a process always observes the effects of its own writes, even on other replicas.

questions.question: In a Dynamo-style system, node B is down when a write destined for it arrives, so node C stores the replica along with metadata naming the intended recipient and forwards it once B recovers. What is this mechanism called?
questions.explanation: Hinted handoff lets a healthy node temporarily hold a replica 'hinted' with the intended owner, preserving write availability during failures.
